title: PyVision-RL: Forging Open Agentic Vision Models via RL
claim: An agent interleaves reasoning and executable code with a runtime, feeding outputs back until answering, with inputs loaded to the runtime first.
layout: Single row, top-to-bottom loop between two bars, dashed divider, color-coded arrows legend
description: A wide horizontal diagram with an orange MLLM bar across the top and a blue Runtime Environment bar across the bottom. On the left, two columns separated by a dashed vertical line show PyVision-Image and PyVision-Video. Each has a green System Prompt box and a purple Hint box (Image Hint or Video Hint). Dark red arrows carry the system prompt up into the MLLM, and for the image case the image hint too. Blue arrows load the hints into the runtime. In the middle, gray boxes labeled code_block_0, mm_clue_0, an ellipsis, code_block_n and mm_clue_n sit on vertical arrows. Down arrows carry code to the runtime and up arrows return clues to the MLLM. A pink Answer box at the right receives a final down arrow. A legend at the bottom explains the blue and dark red arrows.
caption: Agentic scaffolds of \model-RL. We design two agentic scaffolds for image and video understanding under a unified framework of dynamic tooling with Python. For \model-Image, both the system prompt and image hints are injected into the MLLM context, and the images are also loaded into the Python runtime. For \model-Video, only the system prompt is injected into the MLLM context, while the video is loaded exclusively into the runtime environment. Given a query, the model interleaves reasoning with executable code blocks (code\_block\_0) to process multimodal inputs. Execution results (mm\_clue\_0), including textual outputs and rendered images, are appended to the context and fed back to the model. This interaction loop repeats until a final answer is produced. By restricting video inputs first to the runtime, \model-Video enables on-demand context construction, where the agent selectively samples and plots task-relevant frames during reasoning, substantially improving visual token efficiency ([ref]).
abstract: Reinforcement learning for agentic multimodal models often suffers from interaction collapse, where models learn to reduce tool usage and multi-turn reasoning, limiting the benefits of agentic behavior. We introduce PyVision-RL, a reinforcement learning framework for open-weight multimodal models that stabilizes training and sustains interaction. Our approach combines an oversampling-filtering-ranking rollout strategy with an accumulative tool reward to prevent collapse and encourage multi-turn tool use. Using a unified training pipeline, we develop PyVision-Image and PyVision-Video for image and video understanding. For video reasoning, PyVision-Video employs on-demand context construction, selectively sampling task-relevant frames during reasoning to significantly reduce visual token usage. Experiments show strong performance and improved efficiency, demonstrating that sustained interaction and on-demand visual processing are critical for scalable multimodal agents.
